summary: Mira Monte sits in the Ojai Valley of Ventura County, which means the Topa Topa Mountains form a dramatic east-west ridgeline that catches some of the most photographed sunsets in Southern California — yet the community itself is an unincorporated census-designated place of under 7,500 people, often overlooked in favor of its neighbor Ojai just up the road. With a median home value of $827,300 against a median household income of roughly $77,900, the price-to-income ratio lands above 10:1, making ownership a serious stretch without substantial outside equity or dual high-earning households; median rent at $2,060 per month, while steep, consumes a smaller share of income than the purchase math would suggest. The area functions largely as a bedroom community — healthcare and public-sector jobs anchor the local economy, but many commuters head south on Highway 33 toward Ventura, a roughly twenty-minute drive without traffic. Daily highs averaging 71°F and nearly ten hours of sunshine year-round keep the valley's citrus groves and avocado orchards green, and trail access into Los Padres National Forest is minutes away. The poverty rate of 17.5% sits notably above Ventura County's average, a reminder that the valley's beauty and its housing costs create a real affordability tension that the postcard views don't capture.
